510	    # -- inter-node fork sync -------------------------------------------------
511	
512	    SYNC_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50
513	    SYNC_MAX_LIMIT = 200
514	
515	    @staticmethod
516	    def _candidate_blocks(candidate: object) -> object:
517	        """Normalize a sync ``candidate`` to its raw blocks list.
518	
519	        The candidate follows the existing export format (the five-field
520	        ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, blocks}`` document); the
521	        ``{"blocks": [...]}`` wrapper and a bare block list are accepted too.
522	        """
523	        if isinstance(candidate, dict):
524	            return candidate.get("blocks")
525	        return candidate
526	
527	    @staticmethod
528	    def _candidate_fingerprint(blocks_raw: list) -> str:
529	        """Stable content fingerprint of a candidate's raw block list.
530	
531	        Used to decide whether a same-key retry carries the same candidate
532	        content. Key order and whitespace are normalized so two documents that
533	        serialize the same blocks identically compare equal.
534	        """
535	        return hashlib.sha256(
536	            json.dumps(blocks_raw, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
537	        ).hexdigest()
538	
539	    def _prune_expired_syncs(self) -> list[str]:
540	        """Sweep expired sync records and persist the sweep atomically.
541	
542	        A candidate received through a sync lives only while its record is
543	        unexpired; on expiry both the record and its still-stored candidate fork
544	        are dropped, together and in a single atomic save that advances the
545	        generation. Candidates submitted directly (no sync record) never
546	        expire, and an adopted tip is no longer in ``forks`` (it is on the
547	        canonical chain), so its expiring audit record leaves the chain
548	        untouched. If the write fails the pre-cleanup records and forks are
549	        restored so no success is ever reported for an un-persisted sweep.
550	        Caller must hold the store lock. Returns the pruned tip hashes.
551	        """
552	        expired_tips, removed = self.store.prune_syncs()
553	        if not removed:
554	            return expired_tips
555	        removed_forks: dict[str, list] = {}
556	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain}
557	        # The same tip could theoretically be referenced by another live
558	        # record; only drop a fork nothing still points at.
559	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in self.store.syncs.values()}
560	        for tip in expired_tips:
561	            if tip in canonical_hashes or tip in live_tips:
562	                continue
563	            fork = self.store.forks.pop(tip, None)
564	            if fork is not None:
565	                removed_forks[tip] = fork
566	        # Record one permanent expiry event per removed sync record. A tip
567	        # already adopted onto the canonical chain still gets its event: the
568	        # record's expiry is auditable even though the chain is untouched. The
569	        # event freezes the originally delivered summary.
570	        for (rec_source, request_id), rec in sorted(removed.items()):
571	            self.store.append_audit_event(
572	                EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
573	                {
574	                    "source": rec_source,
575	                    "request_id": request_id,
576	                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
577	                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
578	                    "height": rec.get("height"),
579	                    "length": rec.get("length"),
580	                    "status": rec.get("status"),
581	                },
582	            )
583	        try:
584	            self.store.save()

594	    def _tip_descriptor(self, tip_hash: str) -> dict | None:
595	        """Resolve (height/length/status) for a synced tip.
596	
597	        Looks the candidate up among stored forks first, then among canonical
598	        blocks, so audit rows remain available after the candidate is adopted.
599	        """
600	        fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
601	        if fork is not None:
602	            return self._fork_summary(fork)
603	        for block in self.store.chain:
604	            if block.block_hash == tip_hash:
605	                return {
606	                    "tip_hash": block.block_hash,
607	                    "height": block.height,
608	                    # Length counts every block including the genesis block.
609	                    "length": block.height + 1,
610	                    "status": block.status,

614	    def submit_fork_sync(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
615	        """POST /v1/forks/sync — receive a candidate chain from another node.
616	
617	        The request carries ``source``, ``request_id``, ``expires_at`` (Unix
618	        seconds) and ``candidate`` (an export-format fork document).
619	
620	        Authorization. A *new* source+request_id pair is accepted only when the
621	        source is registered in the persistent trust registry with status
622	        ``active`` and an ``expires_at`` still in the future. An unknown,
623	        revoked or registry-expired source is rejected 403 before the candidate
624	        is examined. A retry on a still-live recorded key bypasses the registry
625	        check entirely: the recorded result must keep replaying even after the
626	        source has since been rotated, revoked or expired.
627	
628	        After authorization (and only then) the candidate is re-validated
629	        exactly like a direct candidate submission (canonical genesis,
630	        consecutive heights and prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and
631	        Merkle roots, tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique ascending tx_ids,
632	        endowment replay, pending-only-at-tip).
633	
634	        Status precedence: malformed envelope fields are 400; an unauthorized
635	        source is 403; a well-formed new request whose ``expires_at`` is not
636	        later than now is 410; a well-formed but failing candidate chain (or a
637	        tampered candidate summary) is 400. Returns 201 on first acceptance
638	        with ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, expires_at}``. A retry with
639	        the same source + request_id and identical content replays the original
640	        result as 200; the same key with different content returns 409, as does
641	        a duplicate tip already known.
642	        """
643	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
644	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
645	        for field in ("source", "request_id", "expires_at", "candidate"):
646	            if field not in payload:
647	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
648	
649	        source = payload["source"]
650	        request_id = payload["request_id"]
651	        expires_at = payload["expires_at"]
652	        candidate = payload["candidate"]
653	
654	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
655	            return 400, {"error": "field 'source' must be a non-empty string"}
656	        if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
657	            return 400, {"error": "field 'request_id' must be a non-empty string"}
658	        if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
659	            return 400, {"error": "field 'expires_at' must be a Unix-seconds integer"}
660	
661	        blocks_raw = self._candidate_blocks(candidate)
662	        if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list):
663	            return 400, {"error": "field 'candidate' must contain a 'blocks' list"}
664	
665	        with self.store.lock:
666	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
667	
668	            key = (source, request_id)
669	            existing = self.store.syncs.get(key)
670	
671	            if existing is None:
672	                # Authorization gate for new deliveries only: the source must
673	                # be an active, unexpired entry of the persistent trust
674	                # registry. Unknown, revoked or registry-expired sources are
675	                # refused 403 before the candidate is examined. A retry on a
676	                # still-live key skips this, so a recorded result keeps
677	                # replaying even after the source has since been rotated,
678	                # revoked or expired.
679	                now = time.time()
680	                trusted = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
681	                if (
682	                    trusted is None
683	                    or trusted["status"] != TRUST_ACTIVE
684	                    or trusted["expires_at"] <= now
685	                ):
686	                    return 403, {"error": "source is not an active trusted source"}
687	                # The request's own deadline is checked next, still before the
688	                # candidate chain is examined: a well-formed request whose
689	                # expiry is not later than now is gone (410).
690	                if expires_at <= now:
691	                    return 410, {"error": "sync request has expired"}
692	
693	            # Re-validate the whole candidate chain and recompute the tip
694	            # summary BEFORE any idempotency decision: a request whose supplied
695	            # tip_hash/height/length/status were tampered with must fail 400,
696	            # never be answered with the cached 200 for its source+request_id.
697	            try:
698	                fork = self.store.validate_fork_blocks(blocks_raw)
699	            except ValueError as exc:
700	                return 400, {"error": str(exc)}
701	            summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
702	            if isinstance(candidate, dict):
703	                for field in ("tip_hash", "height", "length", "status"):
704	                    if field in candidate and candidate[field] != summary[field]:
705	                        return 400, {
706	                            "error": f"candidate field {field!r} does not match the blocks"
707	                        }
708	            tip_hash = fork[-1].block_hash
709	            # Fingerprint the *canonicalized* parsed blocks, not the raw
710	            # request list, so recovery (which re-parses the stored fork)
711	            # recomputes an identical fingerprint regardless of insignificant
712	            # serialization differences in the original submission.
713	            canonical_blocks = [block.to_dict() for block in fork]
714	            fingerprint = self._candidate_fingerprint(canonical_blocks)
715	
716	            if existing is not None:
717	                # A retry on a live key is idempotent only when it carries the
718	                # identical candidate content; a changed body conflicts 409.
719	                if fingerprint != existing["fingerprint"]:
720	                    return 409, {
721	                        "error": "request_id already used with different content"
722	                    }
723	                # Replay the ORIGINAL result frozen at first reception; only
724	                # legacy records without a frozen summary resolve live.
725	                descriptor: dict | None = None
726	                if existing.get("height") is not None:
727	                    descriptor = {
728	                        "tip_hash": existing["tip_hash"],
729	                        "height": existing["height"],
730	                        "length": existing["length"],
731	                        "status": existing["status"],
732	                    }
733	                if descriptor is None:
734	                    descriptor = self._tip_descriptor(existing["tip_hash"]) or {
735	                        "tip_hash": existing["tip_hash"],
736	                        "height": None,
737	                        "length": None,
738	                        "status": None,
739	                    }
740	                return 200, {
741	                    "tip_hash": descriptor["tip_hash"],
742	                    "height": descriptor.get("height"),
743	                    "length": descriptor.get("length"),
744	                    "status": descriptor.get("status"),
745	                    "expires_at": existing["expires_at"],
746	                }
747	
748	            if any(tip_hash == block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain):
749	                return 409, {"error": "fork is identical to the canonical chain"}
750	            if tip_hash in self.store.forks:
751	                return 409, {
752	                    "error": "candidate fork already exists",
753	                    "tip_hash": tip_hash,
754	                }
755	
756	            self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
757	            self.store.syncs[key] = {
758	                "tip_hash": tip_hash,
759	                "expires_at": expires_at,
760	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,
761	                # The tip summary is frozen at reception: later adoption or
762	                # expiry never rewrites it, so the history always reports what
763	                # was originally delivered.
764	                "height": summary["height"],
765	                "length": summary["length"],
766	                "status": summary["status"],
767	            }
768	            self.store.append_audit_event(
769	                EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED,
770	                {
771	                    "source": source,
772	                    "request_id": request_id,
773	                    "tip_hash": tip_hash,
774	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
775	                    "height": summary["height"],
776	                    "length": summary["length"],
777	                    "status": summary["status"],
778	                },
779	            )
780	            try:
781	                self.store.save()
782	            except BaseException:
783	                # Roll back the candidate, its metadata and the audit event
784	                # together so a failed write never leaves one without the others.
785	                self.store.syncs.pop(key, None)
786	                self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash, None)
787	                self.store.truncate_audit_events(1)
788	                raise
789	
790	            result = dict(summary)
791	            result["expires_at"] = expires_at
792	            return 201, result

1103	            "public_key": rec["public_key"],

1109	    def _validate_trust_input(self, payload: object, require_version: bool) -> tuple | None:
1110	        """Validate a trust registration/rotation body.
1111	
1112	        ``source`` must be a non-empty string, ``public_key`` 64 lowercase
1113	        hex characters and ``expires_at`` a plain (non-boolean) integer.
1114	        Rotation/revocation additionally require a positive integer
1115	        ``expected_version``. Returns (source, public_key, expires_at[,
1116	        expected_version]) or None after sending a 400.
1117	        """
1118	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
1119	            return None
1120	        for field in ("source", "public_key", "expires_at"):
1121	            if field not in payload:
1122	                return None
1123	        source = payload["source"]
1124	        public_key = payload["public_key"]
1125	        expires_at = payload["expires_at"]
1126	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1127	            return None
1128	        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
1129	            return None

1	"""Persistent storage: blockchain, pending set and derived indexes (JSON).
2	
3	The whole state is one JSON document written atomically: a uniquely named
4	``.ledger-*`` snapshot is fsynced in the same directory and then promoted over
5	the main file with ``os.replace`` (followed by a directory fsync). Every
6	successful write advances a monotonic ``generation`` recorded in the
7	snapshot. A crash can therefore only leave behind (a) the previous main file
8	or (b) a fully fsynced snapshot that never got renamed — never a torn file.
9	
10	On startup the main file and every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
11	as recovery candidates. When no file exists at all, the unique genesis block
12	is created; otherwise each candidate is strictly validated (JSON, generation,
13	consecutive heights, prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and Merkle
14	roots, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signature, pending-only-at-tip and
15	mempool/chain de-duplication). The valid snapshot with the highest generation
16	wins and is promoted if it is still a temp file; same-generation content
17	conflicts, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise StateRecoveryError
18	with the offending path and reason — a fresh chain is never silently created.
19	
20	One atomic write persists everything: the chain (each block carries its
21	confirm/rollback ``status``), a small ``state`` summary, the mempool
22	(``pending``), candidate fork chains (``forks``, each a full block list
23	anchored at the canonical genesis and keyed by its tip hash), the
24	confirmed-transaction ``index`` and the confirmed ``accounts`` activity.
25	Derived data (index/accounts) is *rebuilt* from the chain on every load and
26	every save — pending blocks are excluded, so a restart never resurrects
27	unconfirmed transactions into balances. Persisted fork candidates are
28	re-validated on startup and invalid ones are dropped, while canonical-chain
29	invalidity remains fatal. Each surviving sync record carries the tip summary
30	(height/length/status) frozen at reception; a persisted frozen summary that
31	disagrees with the re-resolved candidate invalidates the record, while a
32	snapshot predating the feature is repaired from its candidate. Persisted sync
33	records are re-verified on restart:
34	records still unexpired whose source stays active and unexpired survive;
35	records whose own deadline elapsed or whose source is unknown/revoked/
36	registry-expired while the process was down are pruned (their non-adopted
37	forks removed; an adopted tip never changes the canonical chain) and each
38	gets exactly one sync_expired audit event backfilled after the durable
39	history, persisted in one atomic write. The backfill deduplicates only
40	within the record's current lifecycle (a durable sync_expired newer than
41	the key's latest sync_received), so a reused (source, request_id) key's
42	new lifecycle is always audited even when every field matches a previous
43	lifecycle's event. Other staleness (a dangling
44	tip or a content-fingerprint mismatch) is a silent prune with no event.
45	A re-entrant lock serializes all updates, and a class-wide recovery lock
46	serializes startup scans against in-flight writes.

123	        """Resolve a descriptor among surviving forks first, then canonical
124	        blocks (the delivered fork may since have been adopted).
125	        """
126	        fork = forks.get(tip_hash)
127	        if fork is not None:
128	            return cls.from_blocks_raw(tip_hash, [block.to_dict() for block in fork])
129	        prefix: list[dict] = []
130	        for block in canonical_chain:
131	            prefix.append(block.to_dict())
132	            if block.block_hash == tip_hash:
133	                return cls.from_blocks_raw(tip_hash, prefix)

207	    # Serializes startup scans/promotions between threads (or two store

212	    def load(self) -> None:
213	        """Recover state from disk on startup.
214	
215	        The main file *and* every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
216	        as recovery candidates. When none exist at all, the unique genesis
217	        block is created (the established first-start convention); otherwise
218	        every candidate is strictly validated and the valid snapshot with the
219	        highest generation wins. A winning temp snapshot is atomically
220	        promoted over the main file and every judged-older or residual
221	        candidate is removed. Same-generation snapshots with conflicting
222	        content, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise
223	        StateRecoveryError — a fresh chain is never silently created.
224	        """
225	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path)) or "."
226	        with self._recovery_lock:
227	            candidates = self._discover_candidates(directory)
228	            if not candidates:
229	                os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
230	                self.chain = [self.create_genesis()]
231	                self.pending = {}
232	                self.forks = {}
233	                self.syncs = {}
234	                self.trust_sources = {}
235	                self.allowlist = {}
236	                self.audit_events = []
237	                self.audit_checkpoint = audit.make_checkpoint([])
238	                # A brand-new node mints its version 1 checkpoint key; the
239	                # first signer is activated at event 0 (the empty log).
240	                self.audit_signer = self._make_audit_signer(1, 0)
241	                self.audit_signer_history = [self._public_signer_entry(self.audit_signer)]
242	                self.generation = 0
243	                self.rebuild_derived()
244	                self.save()
245	                return
246	
247	            valid: list[tuple] = []
248	            errors: list[StateRecoveryError] = []
249	            for candidate in candidates:
250	                try:
251	                    data = self._read_candidate(candidate)
252	                    parsed = self._parse_snapshot(candidate, data)
253	                except StateRecoveryError as exc:
254	                    errors.append(exc)
255	                    continue
256	                # parsed = (chain, pending, generation, forks, initial_balance,
257	                #           syncs, trust_sources, allowlist, audit_events,
258	                #           expired_records, audit_checkpoint, audit_repair,
259	                #           signer_state)
260	                valid.append(
261	                    (
262	                        parsed[2],
263	                        candidate,
264	                        parsed[0],
265	                        parsed[1],
266	                        parsed[3],
267	                        parsed[4],
268	                        parsed[5],
269	                        parsed[6],
270	                        parsed[7],
271	                        parsed[8],
272	                        parsed[9],
273	                        parsed[10],
274	                        parsed[11],
275	                        parsed[12],
276	                    )
277	                )
278	
279	            if not valid:
280	                details = "; ".join(f"{exc.path} ({exc.reason})" for exc in errors)
281	                raise StateRecoveryError(
282	                    directory, f"no valid snapshot candidate found: {details}"
283	                )
284	
285	            max_generation = max(item[0] for item in valid)
286	            top = [item for item in valid if item[0] == max_generation]
287	            # item layout: (generation, path, chain, pending, forks,
288	            # initial_balance, syncs, trust_sources, allowlist, audit_events,
289	            # expired_records, audit_checkpoint, audit_repair, signer_state)
290	            reference = self._canonical_view(
291	                top[0][2],
292	                top[0][3],
293	                top[0][4],
294	                top[0][6],
295	                top[0][7],
296	                top[0][8],
297	                top[0][9],
298	                top[0][5],
299	                top[0][11],
300	                top[0][13][1],
301	            )
302	            for item in top[1:]:
303	                if (
304	                    self._canonical_view(
305	                        item[2],
306	                        item[3],
307	                        item[4],
308	                        item[6],
309	                        item[7],
310	                        item[8],
311	                        item[9],
312	                        item[5],
313	                        item[11],
314	                        item[13][1],
315	                    )
316	                    != reference
317	                ):
318	                    paths = " vs ".join(item[1] for item in top)
319	                    raise StateRecoveryError(
320	                        directory,
321	                        f"conflicting snapshots at generation {max_generation}: {paths}",
322	                    )
323	
324	            # Identical same-generation snapshots: keep the main file when it
325	            # is one of them, avoiding a pointless promotion cycle.
326	            main_abs = os.path.abspath(self.path)
327	            winner = top[0]
328	            for item in top:
329	                if os.path.abspath(item[1]) == main_abs:
330	                    winner = item
331	                    break
332	            (
333	                generation,
334	                winner_path,
335	                chain,
336	                pending,
337	                forks,
338	                winner_init_balance,
339	                syncs,
340	                trust_sources,
341	                allowlist,
342	                audit_events,
343	                expired_records,
344	                audit_checkpoint,
345	                audit_repair,
346	                signer_state,
347	            ) = winner
348	
349	            if os.path.abspath(winner_path) != main_abs:
350	                # The newest durable state only ever made it to a temp
351	                # snapshot (a crash interrupted the promotion): promote it.
352	                os.replace(winner_path, self.path)
353	                self._fsync_dir(directory)
354	
355	            # Reconcile records that expired or lost authorization while the
356	            # process was down, once, on the single winning snapshot: append
357	            # deduplicated sync_expired events with ids continuing after the
358	            # durable history. Doing this after same-generation conflict
359	            # detection keeps that comparison based on durable content (the
360	            # backfill carries a current timestamp).
361	            backfilled = self._backfill_expired_events(audit_events, expired_records)
362	            # A snapshot written before audit hash chaining carries no links;
363	            # expiry backfill events are likewise appended without hashes. In
364	            # both cases the single winning snapshot's log is (re)linked here:
365	            # renumbering dense ids and recomputing reproduces every already
366	            # validated link byte-for-byte and completes the new tail. A
367	            # present-but-wrong chain never reaches this point —
368	            # _parse_snapshot rejects it with StateRecoveryError.
369	            if audit_repair or backfilled:
370	                audit_events = audit.link_events(audit_events)
371	            audit_checkpoint = audit.make_checkpoint(audit_events)
372	
373	            # A pre-checkpoint-auth snapshot carries no signer at all: mint
374	            # its version 1 key once, here, on the unique winner (the
375	            # same-generation conflict comparison above already ran on the
376	            # durable candidates, exactly as for the hash-chain repair). The
377	            # new key is persisted atomically together with the (possibly
378	            # relinked) log and checkpoint in the single save() below.
379	            audit_signer, signer_history, signer_migration = signer_state
380	            if signer_migration:
381	                audit_signer = self._make_audit_signer(1, 0)
382	                signer_history = [self._public_signer_entry(audit_signer)]
383	
384	            self.chain = chain
385	            self.pending = pending
386	            self.forks = forks
387	            self.syncs = syncs
388	            self.trust_sources = trust_sources
389	            self.allowlist = allowlist
390	            self.audit_events = audit_events
391	            self.audit_checkpoint = audit_checkpoint
392	            self.audit_signer = audit_signer
393	            self.audit_signer_history = signer_history
394	            self.generation = generation
395	            # Prefer the endowment recorded by the writer; fall back to the
396	            # value this instance was constructed with, and finally to the
397	            # service default, so older snapshots without the field still
398	            # validate fork replays against the configured endowment.
399	            if winner_init_balance is not None:
400	                self.initial_balance = winner_init_balance
401	            self.rebuild_derived()
402	            self._cleanup_candidates(directory)
403	            # Persist the reconciled state (pruned records/forks + backfilled
404	            # events + legacy hash-chain completion + signer migration)
405	            # atomically so the next restart never re-derives or duplicates
406	            # anything; with nothing to reconcile no write happens and the
407	            # recovered generation is kept byte-for-byte.
408	            if backfilled or audit_repair or signer_migration:
409	                self.save()

411	    def _discover_candidates(self, directory: str) -> list[str]:
412	        """List the main file and sibling .ledger-* snapshots (if any)."""
413	        candidates: list[str] = []
414	        if os.path.exists(self.path):
415	            candidates.append(self.path)
416	        try:
417	            names = sorted(os.listdir(directory))
418	        except OSError:
419	            return candidates
420	        main_name = os.path.basename(self.path)
421	        for name in names:
422	            if name == main_name or not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX):
423	                continue
424	            full = os.path.join(directory, name)
425	            if os.path.isfile(full):
426	                candidates.append(full)
427	        return candidates

429	    @staticmethod
430	    def _canonical_view(
431	        chain: list[Block],
432	        pending: dict[str, Transaction],
433	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
434	        syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] | None = None,
435	        trust_sources: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
436	        allowlist: dict[str, int] | None = None,
437	        audit_events: list[dict] | None = None,
438	        initial_balance: int | None = None,
439	        audit_checkpoint: dict | None = None,
440	        audit_signer_history: list[dict] | None = None,
441	    ) -> str:
442	        """Order-independent canonical content hash for conflict detection.
443	
444	        The recorded ``initial_balance`` is part of the authoritative view: two
445	        same-generation snapshots with identical chains but a different
446	        endowment describe a different replay judgment and must conflict. The
447	        audit checkpoint participates too: two same-generation snapshots with
448	        the same events but a different log head disagree about the audited
449	        state and must conflict. The audit signer history (version, public key,
450	        activation event) participates as well, so a checkpoint key that
451	        differs between two same-generation snapshots is a conflict.
452	        """
453	        sync_records = [
454	            {
455	                "source": key[0],
456	                "request_id": key[1],
457	                "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
458	                "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
459	                "fingerprint": rec["fingerprint"],
460	                "height": rec.get("height"),
461	                "length": rec.get("length"),
462	                "status": rec.get("status"),
463	            }
464	            for key, rec in sorted((syncs or {}).items())
465	        ]
466	        trust_records = [
467	            {"source": source, **rec}
468	            for source, rec in sorted((trust_sources or {}).items())
469	        ]
470	        return json.dumps(
471	            {
472	                "initial_balance": initial_balance,
473	                "chain": [block.to_dict() for block in chain],
474	                "pending": [pending[tx_id].to_dict() for tx_id in sorted(pending)],
475	                "forks": [
476	                    [block.to_dict() for block in forks[tip]]
477	                    for tip in sorted(forks)
478	                ],
479	                "syncs": sync_records,
480	                "trust_sources": trust_records,
481	                "allowlist": dict(sorted((allowlist or {}).items())),
482	                "audit_events": audit_events or [],
483	                "audit_checkpoint": audit_checkpoint
484	                or {"event_id": 0, "event_hash": "0" * 64},
485	                "audit_signer_history": audit_signer_history or [],
486	            },
487	            sort_keys=True,
488	            ensure_ascii=False,
489	        )

491	    def _cleanup_candidates(self, directory: str) -> None:
492	        """Remove every residual .ledger-* snapshot next to the main file.
493	
494	        After recovery these are by definition unusable leftovers: older
495	        generations, an identical post-promotion residue, or a partially
496	        written (invalid) file. The promoted/main state is never touched.
497	        """
498	        main_name = os.path.basename(self.path)
499	        for name in list(os.listdir(directory)):
500	            if not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX) or name == main_name:
501	                continue
502	            full = os.path.join(directory, name)
503	            try:
504	                if os.path.isfile(full) or os.path.islink(full):
505	                    os.unlink(full)
506	            except OSError:
507	                pass
508	        self._fsync_dir(directory)

510	    @staticmethod
511	    def _read_candidate(path: str) -> dict:
512	        """Read and JSON-decode one snapshot file.
513	
514	        Any I/O or JSON failure becomes a StateRecoveryError carrying the
515	        offending path, never a silent fall-back.
516	        """
517	        try:
518	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
519	                data = json.load(fh)
520	        except OSError as exc:
521	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"cannot read file: {exc}") from exc
522	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
523	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"invalid JSON: {exc}") from exc
524	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
525	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "snapshot root must be a JSON object")
526	        return data

528	    def _parse_snapshot(
529	        self, path: str, data: dict
530	    ) -> tuple[
531	        list[Block],
532	        dict[str, Transaction],
533	        int,
534	        dict[str, list[Block]],
535	        int | None,
536	        dict[tuple[str, str], dict],
537	        dict[str, dict],
538	        dict[str, int],
539	        list[dict],
540	        list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
541	        dict,
542	        bool,
543	        tuple[dict | None, list[dict], bool],
544	    ]:
545	        """Strictly validate one decoded snapshot.
546	
547	        Checks the persisted generation, consecutive heights, prev_hash
548	        linkage, recomputed block hashes, recomputed Merkle roots, every
549	        transaction's tx_id and Ed25519 signature, the pending-only-at-tip
550	        rule, and de-duplication between mempool and chain. Returns the parsed
551	        chain, mempool, generation, candidate forks and the recorded initial
552	        balance. Raises StateRecoveryError on the first defect, with ``path``
553	        identifying the candidate.
554	        """
555	        def fail(reason: str) -> None:
556	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, reason)
557	
558	        chain_raw = data.get("chain")
559	        if not isinstance(chain_raw, list) or not chain_raw:
560	            fail("snapshot must contain a non-empty chain")
561	
562	        state = data.get("state")
563	        # A pre-state-section snapshot is accepted: the chain itself is fully
564	        # self-verifying below. A present non-object section is corruption.
565	        if state is None:
566	            state = {}
567	        if not isinstance(state, dict):
568	            fail("invalid 'state' section: must be a JSON object")
569	        generation = state.get("generation", 0)
570	        # bool is an int subclass; reject it explicitly along with negatives.
571	        if isinstance(generation, bool) or not isinstance(generation, int) or generation < 0:
572	            fail("state.generation must be a non-negative integer")
573	        # Schema version gating the one-time pre-checkpoint-auth migration: a
574	        # snapshot written by current code always carries state.version >= 9,
575	        # so a present signer section is mandatory there; only a snapshot whose
576	        # version explicitly predates 9 may lack the signer sections at all.
577	        state_version = state.get("version")
578	        if state_version is not None and (
579	            isinstance(state_version, bool)
580	            or not isinstance(state_version, int)
581	            or state_version < 1
582	        ):
583	            fail("state.version must be a positive integer")
584	        initial_balance = state.get("initial_balance")
585	        if initial_balance is not None and (
586	            isinstance(initial_balance, bool)
587	            or not isinstance(initial_balance, int)
588	            or initial_balance <= 0
589	        ):
590	            fail("state.initial_balance must be a positive integer")
591	
592	        chain: list[Block] = []
593	        seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
594	        for i, block_raw in enumerate(chain_raw):
595	            if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
596	                fail(f"block at position {i} is not a JSON object")
597	            try:
598	                block = Block.from_dict(block_raw)
599	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
600	                fail(f"block {i} is malformed: {exc}")
601	            if block.height != i:
602	                fail(
603	                    f"block at position {i} has non-consecutive height "
604	                    f"{block.height}"
605	                )
606	            expected_prev = GENESIS_PREV_HASH if i == 0 else chain[i - 1].block_hash
607	            if block.prev_hash != expected_prev:
608	                fail(f"block {block.height} has a mismatched prev_hash")
609	            if block.status not in (STATUS_PENDING, STATUS_CONFIRMED):
610	                fail(f"block {block.height} has unknown status {block.status!r}")
611	            if i == 0 and (
612	                block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.transactions
613	            ):
614	                fail("genesis block must be confirmed and carry no transactions")
615	            # Pending blocks may only sit at the chain tip.
616	            if i < len(chain_raw) - 1 and block.status == STATUS_PENDING:
617	                fail(f"pending block {block.height} is not the chain tip")
618	
619	            # Validate every transaction: stored tx_id, recomputed tx_id and
620	            # the Ed25519 signature.
621	            tx_ids: list[str] = []
622	            txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
623	            if not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
624	                fail(f"block {block.height} transactions must be a list")
625	            for j, tx in enumerate(block.transactions):
626	                self._validate_transaction(path, tx)
627	                stored_tx_id = txs_raw[j].get("tx_id") if isinstance(txs_raw[j], dict) else None
628	                if stored_tx_id != tx.tx_id:
629	                    fail(
630	                        f"transaction in block {block.height} has a mismatched "
631	                        f"tx_id (stored {stored_tx_id!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
632	                    )
633	                if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
634	                    fail(
635	                        f"duplicate transaction {tx.tx_id} in block "
636	                        f"{block.height}"
637	                    )
638	                seen_tx_ids.add(tx.tx_id)
639	                tx_ids.append(tx.tx_id)
640	            # Blocks store transactions in ascending tx_id order.
641	            if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
642	                fail(f"block {block.height} transactions are not tx_id sorted")
643	
644	            recomputed_merkle = crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids)
645	            if recomputed_merkle != block.merkle_root:
646	                fail(f"block {block.height} Merkle root mismatch")
647	            recomputed_hash = compute_block_hash(
648	                block.height, block.prev_hash, block.merkle_root
649	            )
650	            if recomputed_hash != block.block_hash:
651	                fail(f"block {block.height} block_hash mismatch")
652	            chain.append(block)
653	
654	        # Mempool: well-formed, no internal duplicates, never overlapping the
655	        # chain (neither confirmed nor pending-block transactions).
656	        pending: dict[str, Transaction] = {}
657	        pending_raw = data.get("pending", [])
658	        if not isinstance(pending_raw, list):
659	            fail("'pending' must be a list")
660	        for tx_raw in pending_raw:
661	            if not isinstance(tx_raw, dict):
662	                fail("pending entry is not a JSON object")
663	            try:
664	                tx = Transaction.from_dict(tx_raw)
665	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
666	                fail(f"pending transaction is malformed: {exc}")
667	            self._validate_transaction(path, tx)
668	            if tx_raw.get("tx_id") != tx.tx_id:
669	                fail(
670	                    f"pending transaction has a mismatched tx_id (stored "
671	                    f"{tx_raw.get('tx_id')!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
672	                )
673	            if tx.tx_id in pending:
674	                fail(f"duplicate pending transaction {tx.tx_id} in mempool")
675	            if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
676	                fail(
677	                    f"pending transaction {tx.tx_id} already exists in a block"
678	                )
679	            pending[tx.tx_id] = tx
680	
681	        # Cross-check the persisted tip summary against the chain tail.
682	        tip = chain[-1]
683	        if state.get("height") is not None and state["height"] != tip.height:
684	            fail("state.height does not match the chain tip")
685	        if state.get("tip_hash") is not None and state["tip_hash"] != tip.block_hash:
686	            fail("state.tip_hash does not match the chain tip")
687	        if (
688	            state.get("tip_status") is not None
689	            and state["tip_status"] != tip.status
690	        ):
691	            fail("state.tip_status does not match the chain tip")
692	
693	        # The recorded endowment is the *only* balance-replay parameter for the
694	        # persisted fork candidates: revalidation below must use it rather than
695	        # this instance's constructor argument, so starting with a different
696	        # --initial-balance can never change a fork's legality. Only a legacy
697	        # snapshot that records no endowment falls back to the configured (then
698	        # the default) value; every snapshot written by current code records it.
699	        replay_endowment = initial_balance
700	        if replay_endowment is None:
701	            replay_endowment = (
702	                self.initial_balance
703	                if self.initial_balance is not None
704	                else DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE
705	            )
706	
707	        forks = self._parse_persisted_forks(
708	            data.get("forks", []), chain, replay_endowment
709	        )
710	        # The trust registry is authoritative configuration and must be parsed
711	        # before the sync records, whose sources are re-authorized against it.
712	        trust_sources = self._parse_persisted_trust_sources(
713	            data.get("trust_sources", []), path
714	        )

716	        # mutated here: same-generation snapshot conflict detection compares
717	        # parsed audit events, and a time-dependent backfill would make two
718	        # byte-identical snapshots look conflicting. The expired-record
719	        # reconciliation returned below is applied once, by load(), to the
720	        # single winning snapshot.

722	            data.get("audit_events", []), path
723	        )

725	            data, audit_events, path
726	        )

728	            state, chain, audit_events, audit_checkpoint, path, state_version
729	        )
730	        syncs, expired_records, synced_tips = self._parse_persisted_syncs(
731	            data.get("syncs", []), forks, chain, trust_sources
732	        )

734	        # that record is gone (expired/unauthorized/invalid on restart):
735	        # without this, the independently-persisted fork would resurrect as a
736	        # never-expiring candidate. Direct submissions carry no sync record and
737	        # are untouched.
738	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in syncs.values()}
739	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in chain}
740	        for tip in synced_tips - live_tips - canonical_hashes:
741	            forks.pop(tip, None)

743	        return (
744	            chain,
745	            pending,
746	            generation,
747	            forks,
748	            initial_balance,
749	            syncs,
750	            trust_sources,
751	            allowlist,
752	            audit_events,
753	            expired_records,
754	            audit_checkpoint,
755	            audit_repair,
756	            signer_state,
757	        )

759	    @staticmethod
760	    def _assess_audit_chain(
761	        data: dict, audit_events: list[dict], path: str
762	    ) -> tuple[dict, bool]:
763	        """Validate the persisted audit hash chain and checkpoint.
764	
765	        Returns ``(checkpoint, needs_repair)``. Three cases:
766	
767	        * a current snapshot with complete hash links: every dense id,
768	          prev_hash link and event_hash is recomputed and the persisted
769	          ``audit_checkpoint`` must pin the exact log head — any mismatch is
770	          snapshot corruption and fails recovery;
771	        * a legacy snapshot predating hash chaining (no link fields, no
772	          checkpoint, or a checkpoint-less section): accepted for a one-time
773	          repair performed by load() on the unique winner; the checkpoint
774	          returned here is the would-be head so same-generation conflict
775	          comparison stays content-based;
776	        * a partially linked log or a present-but-mismatched checkpoint/link:
777	          corruption, never silently repaired.
778	        """
779	        linked_flags = [
780	            isinstance(event, dict)
781	            and ("prev_hash" in event or "event_hash" in event)
782	            for event in audit_events
783	        ]
784	        any_linked = any(linked_flags)
785	        all_linked = all(linked_flags)
786	        checkpoint_raw = data.get("audit_checkpoint")
787	        if any_linked and not all_linked:
788	            raise StateRecoveryError(
789	                path, "audit log is only partially hash-linked"
790	            )
791	        if all_linked and (audit_events or checkpoint_raw is not None):
792	            # A linked log (or an empty log already carrying a checkpoint) is
793	            # strictly verified: links recompute and the checkpoint must pin
794	            # the exact log head.
795	            try:
796	                audit.validate_event_chain(audit_events)
797	            except audit.AuditChainError as exc:
798	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, exc.reason) from exc
799	            if checkpoint_raw is None:
800	                raise StateRecoveryError(
801	                    path, "hash-linked audit log is missing audit_checkpoint"
802	                )
803	            try:
804	                audit.validate_checkpoint(checkpoint_raw, audit_events)
805	            except audit.AuditChainError as exc:
806	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, exc.reason) from exc
807	            return dict(checkpoint_raw), False
808	        # Legacy unlinked log (including a pre-feature empty log with no
809	        # checkpoint). A present checkpoint is inconsistent with an unlinked
810	        # log: treat as corruption rather than silently ignoring it.
811	        if checkpoint_raw is not None:
812	            raise StateRecoveryError(
813	                path, "audit_checkpoint present on an unlinked audit log"
814	            )
815	        linked = audit.link_events(audit_events)
816	        return audit.make_checkpoint(linked), True

818	    def _parse_persisted_audit_signer(
819	        self,
820	        state: dict,
821	        chain: list[Block],
822	        audit_events: list[dict],
823	        audit_checkpoint: dict,
824	        path: str,
825	        state_version: int | None,
826	    ) -> tuple[dict | None, list[dict], bool]:
827	        """Strictly validate the persisted Ed25519 audit checkpoint signer.
828	
829	        Returns ``(current_signer, history, needs_migration)``. The one-time
830	        migration that mints a version 1 key is allowed *only* for a snapshot
831	        whose ``state.version`` explicitly predates 9 and which carries neither
832	        an ``audit_signer`` nor an ``audit_signer_history`` section. When the
833	        version is absent (older than the version field itself is not a
834	        claim current code ever writes) or is 9+, either section missing —
835	        including exactly one of the two — is corruption and fails recovery;
836	        the snapshot is never silently reset to version 1.
837	
838	        A present signer section is strictly verified: the stored seed must
839	        derive the stored public key, the history versions must be dense from
840	        1 with the first activated at event 0, later activation ids must be
841	        strictly ascending and never past the checkpoint, the current record
842	        must equal the latest history entry, every version past 1 must be
843	        activated by an ``audit_signer_rotated`` event whose id, version and
844	        public key match, no orphan rotation events may exist, and a signature
845	        produced by the stored key over the current checkpoint must verify
846	        under its public key. Any defect fails recovery.
847	        """
848	
849	        def fail(reason: str) -> None:
850	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, reason)
851	
852	        raw = state.get("audit_signer")
853	        history_raw = state.get("audit_signer_history")
854	        if raw is None or history_raw is None:
855	            # The two sections are a single unit on every current snapshot.
856	            # Only an explicitly old-version snapshot (state.version < 9) may
857	            # predate both; anything else is corruption, never a reset.
858	            if raw is None and history_raw is not None:
859	                fail("audit_signer_history present without an audit_signer")
860	            if history_raw is None and raw is not None:
861	                fail("audit_signer present without an audit_signer_history")
862	            if state_version is not None and state_version < STATE_VERSION:
863	                return None, [], True
864	            if state_version is None:
865	                fail(
866	                    "snapshot without a state.version is missing both "
867	                    "audit_signer and audit_signer_history"
868	                )
869	            fail(
870	                f"snapshot at state.version {state_version} is missing both "
871	                "audit_signer and audit_signer_history"
872	            )
873	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
874	            fail("state.audit_signer must be an object")
875	        version = raw.get("version")
876	        private_key = raw.get("private_key")
877	        public_key = raw.get("public_key")
878	        activated = raw.get("activated_event_id")
879	        if (
880	            isinstance(version, bool)
881	            or not isinstance(version, int)
882	            or version < 1
883	        ):
884	            fail("audit_signer.version must be a positive integer")
885	        if not crypto.is_hex64(private_key):
886	            fail("audit_signer.private_key must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
887	        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
888	            fail("audit_signer.public_key must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
889	        if crypto.derive_public_key(private_key) != public_key:
890	            fail("audit_signer private_key does not derive its public_key")
891	        if isinstance(activated, bool) or not isinstance(activated, int) or activated < 0:
892	            fail("audit_signer.activated_event_id must be a non-negative integer")
893	        if not isinstance(history_raw, list) or not history_raw:
894	            fail("state.audit_signer_history must be a non-empty list")
895	        history: list[dict] = []
896	        for position, entry in enumerate(history_raw):
897	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
898	                fail("audit_signer_history entry must be an object")
899	            h_version = entry.get("version")
900	            h_public = entry.get("public_key")
901	            h_activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
902	            if (
903	                isinstance(h_version, bool)
904	                or not isinstance(h_version, int)
905	                or h_version != position + 1
906	            ):
907	                fail("audit_signer_history versions must be dense from 1")
908	            if not crypto.is_hex64(h_public):
909	                fail("audit_signer_history public_key must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
910	            if (
911	                isinstance(h_activated, bool)
912	                or not isinstance(h_activated, int)
913	                or h_activated < 0
914	            ):
915	                fail("audit_signer_history activated_event_id must be non-negative")
916	            if position == 0 and h_activated != 0:
917	                fail("the first audit signer must be activated at event 0")
918	            if position > 0 and h_activated <= history[-1]["activated_event_id"]:
919	                fail("audit signer activation ids must be strictly ascending")
920	            history.append(
921	                {
922	                    "version": h_version,
923	                    "public_key": h_public,
924	                    "activated_event_id": h_activated,
925	                }
926	            )
927	        latest = history[-1]
928	        if (
929	            version != latest["version"]
930	            or public_key != latest["public_key"]
931	            or activated != latest["activated_event_id"]
932	        ):
933	            fail("current audit_signer does not match the latest history entry")
934	        if activated > audit_checkpoint["event_id"]:
935	            fail("audit signer activated beyond the checkpoint")
936	
937	        # Every version past 1 must be explained by an audit_signer_rotated
938	        # event at its activation id, carrying the same version and public
939	        # key; every such event must in turn match a history entry.
940	        rotated_by_id: dict[int, dict] = {}
941	        for event in audit_events:
942	            if event.get("kind") != EVENT_AUDIT_SIGNER_ROTATED:
943	                continue
944	            rotated_by_id[event["event_id"]] = event
945	        for entry in history[1:]:
946	            event = rotated_by_id.pop(entry["activated_event_id"], None)
947	            if event is None:
948	                fail(
949	                    f"audit signer version {entry['version']} has no matching "
950	                    "audit_signer_rotated event"
951	                )
952	            if (
953	                event.get("version") != entry["version"]
954	                or event.get("public_key") != entry["public_key"]
955	            ):
956	                fail(
957	                    f"audit_signer_rotated event {event['event_id']} does not "
958	                    "match the signer history"
959	                )
960	        if rotated_by_id:
961	            fail("orphan audit_signer_rotated event with no signer history entry")
962	
963	        # Re-verify the signature material over the recovered checkpoint: a
964	        # signature produced by the stored seed must verify under its public
965	        # key and the recorded activation, pinning this deployment's genesis.
966	        signature = audit.sign_checkpoint_auth(
967	            private_key,
968	            chain[0].block_hash,
969	            audit_checkpoint,
970	            version,
971	        )
972	        if not signature or not audit.verify_checkpoint_auth(
973	            public_key,
974	            chain[0].block_hash,
975	            audit_checkpoint,
976	            version,
977	            signature,
978	        ):
979	            fail("audit checkpoint signer failed signature re-verification")
980	
981	        current = {
982	            "version": version,
983	            "private_key": private_key,
984	            "public_key": public_key,
985	            "activated_event_id": activated,
986	        }
987	        return current, history, False

989	    @staticmethod
990	    def _backfill_expired_events(
991	        audit_events: list[dict],
992	        expired_records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
993	    ) -> int:
994	        """Append one sync_expired event per down-time-expired sync record.
995	
996	        Mirrors the runtime sweep exactly: records are processed in
997	        ``(source, request_id)`` order, each gets a dense event_id continuing
998	        after the durable history, and every *lifecycle removal* gets its own
999	        event. Deduplication is lifecycle-aware, never identity-based across
1000	        lifecycles: a durable sync_expired covers the persisted record only
1001	        when it sits after the latest sync_received for the same
1002	        ``(source, request_id)`` key — i.e. it belongs to the record's
1003	        current lifecycle (the crash-interrupted-cleanup case). An expiry
1004	        event from an *earlier* lifecycle of a reused key never suppresses
1005	        the new lifecycle's event, even when source, request_id, tip_hash
1006	        and expires_at are all identical. Returns the number of events
1007	        appended. Mutates ``audit_events`` in place.
1008	        """
1009	        # Position of the latest sync_received per key: it opens the
1010	        # lifecycle every later event of that key belongs to.
1011	        last_received: dict[tuple[object, object], int] = {}
1012	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
1013	            if event.get("kind") == EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED:
1014	                last_received[(event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"))] = index
1015	        # Identities already expired *within their current lifecycle*.
1016	        covered: set[tuple[object, object, object]] = set()
1017	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
1018	            if event.get("kind") != EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED:
1019	                continue
1020	            key = (event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"))
1021	            if index > last_received.get(key, -1):
1022	                covered.add((key[0], key[1], event.get("tip_hash")))
1023	        backfilled = 0
1024	        for source, request_id, rec in sorted(
1025	            expired_records, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1])
1026	        ):
1027	            identity = (source, request_id, rec["tip_hash"])
1028	            if identity in covered:
1029	                continue
1030	            event = {
1031	                "event_id": len(audit_events) + 1,
1032	                "kind": EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
1033	                "at": time.time(),
1034	                "source": source,
1035	                "request_id": request_id,
1036	                "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
1037	                "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
1038	            }
1039	            # Freeze the delivered summary when recovery could resolve it;
1040	            # records in snapshots older than the frozen-summary feature may
1041	            # not carry one, in which case the history query resolves live.
1042	            if rec.get("height") is not None:
1043	                event["height"] = rec["height"]
1044	                event["length"] = rec.get("length")
1045	                event["status"] = rec.get("status")
1046	            audit_events.append(event)
1047	            covered.add(identity)
1048	            backfilled += 1
1049	        return backfilled

1051	    @staticmethod
1052	    def _parse_persisted_trust_sources(
1053	        raw: object, path: str
1054	    ) -> dict[str, dict]:
1055	        """Strictly parse the persisted source-trust registry.
1056	
1057	        Unlike candidate forks (re-validated and silently dropped when stale),
1058	        the trust registry is authoritative configuration: a malformed entry
1059	        is snapshot corruption and fails recovery rather than being dropped.
1060	        Each record needs a non-empty source, a 64-char lowercase hex public
1061	        key, an integer expiry, a positive integer version and a known status.
1062	        """
1063	        if raw is None:
1064	            return {}
1065	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1066	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'trust_sources' must be a list")
1067	        sources: dict[str, dict] = {}
1068	        for entry in raw:
1069	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
1070	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source entry must be an object")
1071	            source = entry.get("source")
1072	            public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1073	            expires_at = entry.get("expires_at")
1074	            version = entry.get("version")
1075	            status = entry.get("status")
1076	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1077	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source must be a non-empty string")
1078	            if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
1079	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1080	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has an invalid public_key"
1081	                )
1082	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
1083	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1084	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} expires_at must be an integer"
1085	                )
1086	            if (
1087	                isinstance(version, bool)
1088	                or not isinstance(version, int)
1089	                or version < 1
1090	            ):
1091	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1092	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} version must be a positive integer"
1093	                )
1094	            if status not in (TRUST_ACTIVE, TRUST_REVOKED):
1095	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1096	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has invalid status {status!r}"
1097	                )
1098	            if source in sources:
1099	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1100	                    path, f"duplicate trust source {source!r} in snapshot"
1101	                )
1102	            sources[source] = {
1103	                "public_key": public_key,
1104	                "expires_at": expires_at,
1105	                "version": version,
1106	                "status": status,
1107	            }
1108	        return sources

1191	                    )

1193	                if expires_at is not None and (
1194	                    isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int)
1195	                ):
1196	                    raise StateRecoveryError(
1197	                        path,
1198	                        f"audit event {event_id} ({kind}) expires_at must be an integer",
1199	                    )
1200	                height = event.get("height")
1201	                if height is not None and (
